candidates: When adding a `schedule:` cron trigger in any GitHub Actions workflow file, use a non-zero minute offset (e.g., `28 3 * * *`) rather than scheduling at the exact top of the hour (minute `0`). GitHub's own documentation warns that on-the-hour schedules face higher risk of being delayed or dropped due to scheduler congestion.

When a GitHub Actions workflow step commits files back to the repository (e.g., using `EndBug/add-and-commit` or any equivalent action), explicitly set the commit author to the GitHub Actions bot identity: `author_name: 'github-actions[bot]'` and `author_email: '41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com'`. Without this, scheduled workflow runs attribute commits to the repository owner's personal account rather than the bot.
